column1: In the last decade a revolution has occurred in the way that scientists think about the brain.
column2: 过去十年间，科学家看待大脑的方式发生了根本性的变化。
column3: in the last decade|在过去十年里

column1: We now know that the decisions humans make can be traced to the firing patterns of neurons in specific parts of the brain.
column2: 我们现在知道，人作出的决策可以追溯到大脑特定区域神经元的放电模式。
column4: can be traced to|可以追溯到

column1: These discoveries have led to the field known as neuroeconomics, which studies the brain’s secrets to success in an economic environment that demands innovation and being able to do things differently from competitors.
column2: 这些发现催生了神经经济学。它研究的是，在既要求创新、又要求做法有别于竞争对手的经济环境中，大脑有哪些奥秘能帮助人取得成功。
column7: secrets to success|n. 成功的奥秘

column1: A brain that can do this is an iconoclastic one.
column2: 有这种能力的大脑，能够打破思维常规。

column1: Briefly, an iconoclast is a person who does something that others say can’t be done.
column2: 简言之，打破常规的人，能做成别人断言做不成的事。

column1: This definition implies that iconoclasts are different from other people, but more precisely, it is their brains that are different in three distinct ways: perception, fear response, and social intelligence.
column2: 按这个定义，打破常规的人与别人有所不同。更准确地说，是他们的大脑在三个方面有别于常人：知觉、恐惧反应和社交智力。
column7: three distinct ways|n. 三个不同方面

column1: Each of these three functions utilizes a different circuit in the brain.
column2: 这三项功能各自动用大脑中不同的神经回路。
column6: different circuit|n. 不同的神经回路

column1: Naysayers might suggest that the brain is irrelevant, that thinking in an original, even revolutionary, way is more a matter of personality than brain function.
column2: 持反对意见的人或许会说，这与大脑无关。能否以独创的、甚至革命性的方式思考，更多取决于个性，而较少取决于大脑的功能。
column8: more a matter of|更多取决于

column1: But the field of neuroeconomics was born out of the realization that the physical workings of the brain place limitations on the way we make decisions.
column2: 不过，神经经济学之所以出现，是因为人们认识到，大脑的生理运作机制制约着我们作决策的方式。
column7: physical workings|n. 生理运作机制

column1: By understanding these constraints, we begin to understand why some people march to a different drumbeat.
column2: 了解了这些限制，我们便开始明白，为什么有些人会按自己的方式行事。
column5: march to a different drumbeat|以自己的方式行事

column1: The first thing to realize is that the brain suffers from limited resources.
column2: 首先要认识到，大脑能动用的资源有限。
column3: first thing to realize|首先要认识到的事

column1: It has a fixed energy budget, about the same as a 40 watt light bulb, so it has evolved to work as efficiently as possible.
column2: 大脑可用的能量是有限额的，耗能大约相当于一只40瓦的灯泡。因此，它逐渐演化出尽可能高效的运作方式。
column3: fixed energy budget|n. 固定的能量限额
column4: about the same as|大致相当于
column5: 40 watt light bulb|n. 四十瓦的灯泡
column7: as efficiently as possible|尽可能高效地

column1: This is where most people are impeded from being an iconoclast.
column2: 正是这一点，使大多数人很难成为打破常规的人。

column1: For example, when confronted with information streaming from the eyes, the brain will interpret this information in the quickest way possible.
column2: 例如，面对从双眼不断涌入的信息，大脑会以尽可能快的方式作出解读。
column4: information streaming from|从……不断涌入的信息
column6: quickest way possible|尽可能快捷的方式

column1: Thus it will draw on both past experience and any other source of information, such as what other people say, to make sense of what it is seeing.
column2: 因此，大脑会利用以往经验和其他一切可用的信息来源，例如别人所说的话，来理解眼前所见。
column6: source of information|n. 信息来源

column1: This happens all the time.
column2: 这种情况随时都在发生。

column1: The brain takes shortcuts that work so well we are hardly ever aware of them.
column2: 大脑会走捷径。这些捷径十分管用，以至于我们几乎从来意识不到它们。

column1: We think our perceptions of the world are real, but they are only biological and electrical rumblings.
column2: 我们以为自己感知到的就是真实世界，但这些知觉其实只是大脑里生物活动和电活动造成的动静。
column8: rumblings|n. 内部活动产生的动静

column1: Perception is not simply a product of what your eyes or ears transmit to your brain.
column2: 知觉并不只是眼睛或耳朵传给大脑的信息所产生的结果。

column1: More than the physical reality of photons or sound waves, perception is a product of the brain.
column2: 相比于光子或声波这些物理现象，知觉更多地是大脑活动的产物。

column1: Perception is central to iconoclasm.
column2: 知觉是打破常规的关键。
column5: iconoclasm|n. 打破常规的思维方式

column1: Iconoclasts see things differently to other people.
column2: 打破常规的人看待事物的方式与别人不同。

column1: Their brains do not fall into efficiency pitfalls as much as the average person’s brain.
column2: 与普通人的大脑相比，他们的大脑较少陷入一味求快的陷阱。
column4: efficiency pitfalls|n. 过分追求效率所造成的陷阱

column1: Iconoclasts, either because they were born that way or through learning, have found ways to work around the perceptual shortcuts that plague most people.
column2: 打破常规的人，或是天生如此，或是经后天学习，已经找到了绕开那些困扰多数人的知觉捷径的办法。
column4: were born that way|天生如此

column1: Perception is not something that is hardwired into the brain.
column2: 知觉并非大脑与生俱来便已设定好的东西。

column1: It is a learned process, which is both a curse and an opportunity for change.
column2: 知觉是通过学习形成的。这一点既带来困扰，也给改变留下了机会。
column3: learned process|n. 通过学习形成的过程
column6: opportunity for change|n. 改变的机会

column1: The brain faces the fundamental problem of interpreting physical stimuli from the senses.
column2: 大脑面临的一个基本问题就是如何解读来自感官的物理刺激。

column1: Everything the brain sees, hears, or touches has multiple interpretations.
column2: 无论大脑看到、听到还是触碰到什么，都有不止一种解释。

column1: The one that is ultimately chosen is simply the brain’s best theory.
column2: 最终选定的那种解释，不过是大脑认为最说得通的一种推测。

column1: In technical terms, these conjectures have their basis in the statistical likelihood of one interpretation over another and are heavily influenced by past experience and, importantly for potential iconoclasts, what other people say.
column2: 从技术上说，这些推测的依据是，从统计角度看，某一种解释比另一种更有可能成立。过去的经验会对这些推测产生很大影响。别人的话同样有很大影响，这一点对可能打破常规的人尤其重要。
column5: have their basis in|以……为依据
column6: statistical likelihood|统计意义上的可能性

column1: The best way to see things differently to other people is to bombard the brain with things it has never encountered before.
column2: 要以不同于他人的方式看待事物，最好的办法是让大脑不断接触以前从未遇到过的事物。
column3: see things differently|以不同的方式看待事物
column4: bombard the brain with|让大脑大量、反复接触

column1: Novelty releases the perceptual process from the chains of past experience and forces the brain to make new judgments.
column2: 新事物使知觉过程摆脱过往经验的束缚，并迫使大脑作出新的判断。

column1: Successful iconoclasts have an extraordinary willingness to be exposed to what is fresh and different.
column2: 成功打破常规的人格外愿意接触新鲜而不同的事物。
column3: Successful iconoclasts|n. 成功打破常规的人
column4: extraordinary willingness|n. 非同寻常的意愿
column6: fresh and different|新鲜而不同的

column1: Observation of iconoclasts shows that they embrace novelty while most people avoid things that are different.
column2: 观察这些打破常规的人就会发现，他们乐于接受新事物，而多数人会避开与平常不同的东西。

column1: The problem with novelty, however, is that it tends to trigger the brain’s fear system.
column2: 然而，新事物有一个问题：它往往会触发大脑的恐惧系统。

column1: Fear is a major impediment to thinking like an iconoclast and stops the average person in his tracks.
column2: 恐惧是打破思维常规的一大障碍，常人会因此止步不前。
column6: in his tracks|当场，令其止步

column1: There are many types of fear, but the two that inhibit iconoclastic thinking and people generally find difficult to deal with are fear of uncertainty and fear of public ridicule.
column2: 恐惧有很多种，其中有两种会抑制打破常规的思考，而且人们普遍难以应对：害怕不确定性，害怕当众遭人嘲笑。
column4: iconoclastic thinking|n. 打破常规的思考
column8: public ridicule|n. 当众受到的嘲笑

column1: These may seem like trivial phobias.
column2: 这些惧怕似乎都算不上什么大事。

column1: But fear of public speaking, which everyone must do from time to time, afflicts one-third of the population.
column2: 然而，人人都不时需要当众讲话，而对当众讲话的恐惧却困扰着三分之一的人。

column1: This makes it too common to be considered a mental disorder.
column2: 这种恐惧太普遍了，因而不能算作一种精神障碍。

column1: It is simply a common variant of human nature, one which iconoclasts do not let inhibit their reactions.
column2: 这只是人性中一种常见的表现，打破常规的人不会让这种恐惧妨碍自己作出反应。
column4: common variant|n. 常见的一种表现形式

column1: Finally, to be successful iconoclasts, individuals must sell their ideas to other people.
column2: 最后，要成为成功的破格创新者，还必须说服别人接受自己的想法。
column7: sell their ideas|说服别人接受自己的想法

column1: This is where social intelligence comes in.
column2: 这正是社交智力发挥作用的地方。

column1: Social intelligence is the ability to understand and manage people in a business setting.
column2: 社交智力，就是在商业环境中理解和管理他人的能力。

column1: In the last decade there has been an explosion of knowledge about the social brain and how the brain works when groups coordinate decision making.
column2: 过去十年，人们对社会脑的认识迅速增长，也越来越了解群体协调决策时大脑如何运作。
column4: explosion of knowledge|知识的迅速增长

column1: Neuroscience has revealed which brain circuits are responsible for functions like understanding what other people think, empathy, fairness, and social identity.
column2: 神经科学已经揭示，理解他人的想法、共情、公平感和社会认同等功能分别由哪些脑回路负责。

column1: These brain regions play key roles in whether people convince others of their ideas.
column2: 一个人能否说服别人接受自己的想法，这些脑区起着关键作用。
column6: convince others of|说服他人相信

column1: Perception is important in social cognition too.
column2: 在社会认知中，知觉也很重要。

column1: The perception of someone’s enthusiasm, or reputation, can make or break a deal.
column2: 你怎么看对方的热忱或声誉，可能决定一桩交易成不成。

column1: Understanding how perception becomes intertwined with social decision making shows why successful iconoclasts are so rare.
column2: 弄清知觉如何与社会决策交织在一起，就能明白为什么成功打破常规的人如此少见。
column5: social decision making|n. 社会决策
column6: successful iconoclasts|n. 成功打破常规的人

column1: Iconoclasts create new opportunities in every area from artistic expression to technology to business.
column2: 打破常规的人在各个领域都能开创新机会，从艺术表达、技术到商业皆是如此。

column1: They supply creativity and innovation not easily accomplished by committees.
column2: 他们能贡献创造力，推动创新，而这些往往是委员会难以做到的。

column1: Rules aren’t important to them.
column2: 对他们来说，规则并不重要。

column1: Iconoclasts face alienation and failure, but can also be a major asset to any organization.
column2: 打破常规的人面临被孤立和失败的风险，但也能成为任何组织的宝贵人才。
column7: major asset|n. 极有价值的人才

column1: It is crucial for success in any field to understand how the iconoclastic mind works.
column2: 要在任何领域取得成功，了解善于打破常规的人如何思考都至关重要。
